ALBUM VIEWABLE_ITEM_IDS UNIFICATION VERIFIED ACROSS SHORTCODE AND BLOCK, item-for-item. Fresh album 288 (owner journey_owner/106, privacy public) seeded with one public item (media 67626) and one private item (media 67627), both owned by 106, both added via AlbumService::add_items() so the real mvs_album_items membership table is exercised, not just the index's album_id column. [mvs_collection] CONTAINER GATE VERIFIED, both privacy levels. PRO CONNECTOR-PREFS REGISTRY GUARD VERIFIED LIVE. Connectors are off by default on this site (option absent, falls back to '0'); mvs_connectors_enabled was set to '1' for the probe via wp option update - registering the real Flickr connector through Plugin::init()'s existing wiring, not a test-only filter - and the option was deleted back to absent afterward. As journey_other (subscriber) with a live wp_rest cookie nonce, POST action=mvs_save_connector_prefs&connector=probe-arbitrary-key to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php returned 404 {"message":"Unknown connector."} and wrote zero mvs_connector_* user_meta rows, confirmed by direct query. The same POST with connector=flickr (now present in the registry) returned 200 {success:true, updated:{auto_export,default_privacy}} and the meta was written, then deleted afterward. The registry check does real work: an unrecognised id cannot mint arbitrary mvs_connector_{anything}_* meta on the caller's own account, and a real connector still saves.

CWE-863 BYPASS CLOSED, verified on an ARMED private community rather than against the gate function. Arming it needed care worth recording: mvs_rest_require_auth already carries 14 callbacks on this site and BuddyNext answers 'public' late, so a probe added at the default priority is overruled and every route answers 200 - which looks exactly like a still-open bypass. The probe had to run at PHP_INT_MAX before the gate armed at all. With it armed and signed out, all ten casings are refused with 401 mvs_community_private: /mvs/v1/albums, /MVS/v1/albums, /mvs/V1/albums, /MVS/V1/ALBUMS, /mvs/v1/media, /mvs/V1/media, /MvS/v1/media, /mVs/V1/Media, and Pro's /mvs-pro/v1/documents and /MVS-PRO/v1/documents. Before the fix the reporter saw /MVS/v1/albums return 200 with 9 albums and /mvs/V1/media 200 with 20 items; both are now 401.

THE EXEMPTION RISK - the one that would have been worse than the bug - DOES NOT MATERIALISE. On an armed private community a signed media URL still delivers: the original and the large thumbnail both return HTTP 200 image/jpeg at 84760 bytes, signed out, and they do so in every namespace casing tried (mvs/v1, MVS/v1, mvs/V1, MVS/V1, and MvS/v1/SERVE), because the exemption list is lower-cased alongside the route. /app/config likewise answers 200 in three casings, which keeps private-community mode enterable from a native client. The exemption has not become a bypass: a tampered signature is 403, an expired one is 403 and an unsigned request is 400, and the boundary match holds - /mvs/v1/app/configuration, /mvs/v1/app/configx and /mvs/v1/serveeeee are all 401 rather than inheriting the exemption they resemble. MOST IMPORTANTLY, a LOGGED-IN MEMBER on an armed private community browses normally: Explore 14 of 14 images loaded, profile 20 of 20, My Media 10 of 11, with ZERO failed wp-json or /serve requests and zero console errors, and member REST (/media, /albums, /me/media, /me/notifications and Pro /documents) all 200. The single non-loading image is a hidden empty-src Interactivity template placeholder (data-wp-bind--src, offsetParent null) that predates this work and is invisible to users. Media is not broken for members.

MVS_CSS NON-SCALAR GUARD VERIFIED, and the block CSS path still works. generate() by id type: 'abc123', 123, 1.5, true and '0042' each still produce their selector (.mvs-block-abc123, .mvs-block-123, .mvs-block-15, .mvs-block-1, .mvs-block-0042); null, '', 0, an array and an object all return an empty string. ZERO warnings raised across all ten, where an array id previously emitted 'Array to string conversion' at MVS_CSS.php:68 and a '.mvs-block-Array' selector - that debug_log_issues entry is now cleared. The footer path behaves: add() with two real ids plus a hostile array id and a null id buffers exactly 2 styles, and output() emits <style id="mvs-block-styles"> carrying both correct selectors, no mvs-block-Array and no angle bracket. Note the guard also protects add() itself, which indexes self::$styles by the id - an array id would have been an illegal offset there too. Pre-existing and unchanged by this patch: an id of 0 or '0' is rejected by the empty() half of the condition, which is fine because uniqueIds are generated hashes.

END-TO-END ON A REAL PAGE, which is what the guard could have broken. A published page carrying mvs/media-grid (uniqueId qaGuard01, padding 12/14/16/18px, margin 2rem) and mvs/media-stats (uniqueId qaGuard02, padding 7em) renders HTTP 200 with the footer <style id="mvs-block-styles"> present, both selectors emitted, both wrapper elements carrying the matching .mvs-block-<uid> class, and the rules actually APPLIED - computed padding-top reads 12px on the first block and 119px on the second (7em against a 17px root). No mvs-block-Array, no angle bracket inside the style element, no PHP notice in the body and no console error. One thing worth recording so it is not misread as a regression: as an ANONYMOUS visitor the media-stats block contributes no CSS and no wrapper class, because src/blocks/media-stats/render.php returns early at line 17 before it ever reaches MVS_CSS::add() at line 80. That is pre-existing behaviour, not the guard - the same block buffers its style correctly the moment it renders for a capable user. The test page was deleted afterwards.

RESOLVED, the download response-shape change flagged at the 12:32 stamp is SAFE and needs no client update - verified independently rather than taken on report. src/blocks/shared-ui/view.js:1817 is the ONLY JavaScript caller of POST /media/{id}/download; it awaits inside a try/catch explicitly commented as a best-effort, non-blocking stat increment and DISCARDS the return value, so nothing reads .views or .downloads off that endpoint. The other .views readers in the codebase are unaffected: media-social/view.js:118 reads data.views from the VIEW endpoint, whose payload is unchanged, and shared-ui/view.js:578 reads a stats object. No consumer needs updating; the rename from views to downloads on the deduped download reply is purely a correctness fix.

SECURITY RE-CUT VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, every hole re-tested from the caller's side rather than from the diff. (1) GET /media/{id}/group, the metadata leak: anonymous and a second member at the same role both get 404 mvs_not_found for a private item and for a private item inside a group, with no title, description or owner in the body; the members-scope item is 404 for anonymous and 200 for a signed-in member; the owner sees everything. The per-member filter is the part that matters and it holds - the public gallery containing one private photo returns ONLY the public id to anonymous and to the other member, and both ids to the owner. 404 rather than 403 throughout, so there is no existence oracle. (2) POST /media/{id}/chapters: owner 200, same-role author 403 mvs_pro_forbidden, subscriber 403, anonymous 401 mvs_pro_unauthorized, admin with moderate_mvs_media 200 - and the refused writes left the stored chapters untouched. Note the first attempt at this test used the wrong payload shape and returned 400 for everyone, which proves nothing about authority; the matrix above is from a schema-valid payload. (3) can_read_media() now resolves privacy: with the video flipped private, chapter reads are 200 for the owner and 404 mvs_pro_not_found for the same-role author, the subscriber and anonymous, with no chapter titles in any refused body. (4) MVS_CSS: a paddingUnit and a marginUnit of "px} </style><script>alert(document.domain)</script><style>" both fall back to px, and the generated CSS contains no angle bracket and no 'script' substring; an unknown unit ('parsecs') falls back too and a legal one ('rem') is honoured. (5) Range clamping over HTTP on a 5065-byte file: bytes=0-999999999 and bytes=0- both return 206 with Content-Length 5065 and Content-Range bytes 0-5064/5065; bytes=0-99 returns 100; bytes=5000-999999 clamps to 65; bytes=99999-100000 returns 416 with Content-Range bytes */5065. Content-Length equalled the delivered body in every case, which is the bug. (6) StorageResolver::safe_stored_name(): report.pdf.php, shell.php, evil.phtml, x.php5, a.PHP, t.phar, script.js and page.html all gain .bin; doc.pdf, sheet.xlsx, notes.md and archive.tar.gz are untouched; weird.php.pdf becomes weird.php_.pdf. A file with no extension also gains .bin, which is harmless because the on-disk name is internal.

VIEW-COUNTER DEDUP REFACTOR RE-RUN, the change flagged as riskiest because it touched a counter that already worked. Sequence as one signed-in member against a fresh fixture: view #1 recorded; view #2 inside the window counted:false with views:1; download #1 WITH A PRIOR VIEW ALREADY PRESENT recorded:true - this is the exact case the old code got wrong, because its dedup asked for 'view' rows, so the download was dropped whenever the visitor had merely viewed the item; download #2 counted:false with downloads:1; view #3 still counted:false with views:1, so view dedup was not broken by the refactor; share #1 recorded:true and share #2 recorded:false, the new transient dedup. Database after the sequence: exactly one 'view' row and one 'download' row for that user, and stats views=1 downloads=1 shares=1 - every event counted once and only once. Downloads are disabled site-wide by default (mvs_allow_downloads), so the option was enabled for this test and restored to its original empty value afterwards; without that step the download leg silently returns 403 and the riskiest path goes untested. CONTRACT CHANGE WORTH ANNOUNCING: the deduped download reply now reports 'downloads' where it previously reported 'views'. That is the fix, but it is a response-shape change shipping in a patch, so any client reading .views off the download endpoint will need updating.

NOT EXERCISED THIS ROUND, and therefore not evidenced: the Pro connector export ownership check. The guard itself reads correctly - it compares media_repository->get_author($media_id) against the calling user and allows moderate_mvs_media through, and get_author() was confirmed to return the true owner id for three sampled items - but ConnectorRESTController's routes are NOT REGISTERED on this site (no /mvs-pro/v1/connectors/* appears in the route index, because the controller is only wired when connectors are configured), so no live request could reach it. It needs a site with a connected remote account: a member requesting export of another member's media id must be refused with 'You can only export your own media.' and must not stamp external_source or external_id onto the victim's row. Counted as skipped, not passed.

ALBUM PICKER SCOPING CONFIRMED, AND IT IS NOT A PRIVACY FIX. With author=<viewer> the REST response carries only the viewer's own albums and no other member's titles: mina_aoki gets exactly [Tokyo Streets, author 8], admin gets exactly [Field Notes, author 1]. Worth being precise about what changed: the scoping is client-side - the picker now sends the parameter - and an unscoped GET /mvs/v1/albums still returns every album a viewer is allowed to see, which for this fixture is nine public albums including other members' titles. That is not a leak, and I probed it: flipping album 238 to private removed it from BOTH another member's and an anonymous visitor's unscoped listing (8 items, 238 absent), so the endpoint is privacy-gated server-side and the picker change is a UX scoping improvement on top of it. Album 238 restored to public.

B_upgrade remains skipped: no prior-version install was staged. The Docker work proved the FRESH-install path only. B1/B2/B3 still want a 2.5.0 install upgraded in place to confirm the migration runs quietly, the Pro option-prefix migration is idempotent, and schema additions back-fill - which now also means confirming an upgraded site KEEPS comment_count while a new one does not, the one assertion this round could only prove from two separate installs rather than one upgrade.

PRECONDITION TO ADD TO THE RUNBOOK - assert src vs build parity before a walk. Pro blocks register from MVS_PRO_DIR . 'build/blocks/' (includes/Blocks/BlockRegistrar.php:73-80), and build/ is gitignored (wpmediaverse-pro/.gitignore:23). It is refreshed only by an explicit build, so a clean git tree says nothing about what the site actually renders and the walked site can silently lag the source. That is exactly what happened with pro-document-embed: the fix was correct in src/ but build/ still held the pre-fix file, so the row read as a broken fix for a whole round trip. Packaging does run grunt build -> npm run build:blocks, so the zip would have shipped correct code - the risk is QA certifying a build the release does not contain, in either direction. Suggested check at the top of Global preconditions: for each src/blocks/*/render.php compare against build/blocks/<slug>/render.php and STOP if any differ, the same way a failing fixture cleanup is treated as a release blocker.

RUNBOOK MAINTENANCE DEBT - the runbook's own rule is that every customer-visible fix ships with a matching D row in the same PR. RUNBOOK CORRECTIONS the next editor should apply (verified against 2.5.1 code, not defects): (1) C.anon.single-media claims /p/<media_id>/ is the canonical MVS URL - it is not. /p/([0-9]+) is BuddyNext's route (buddynext/includes/Core/PageRouter.php:2358), so /p/<mvs media id>/ correctly 404s. MVS's own route is /media/<slug>/ -> mvs_media_slug, which BuddyNext redirects via the documented mvs_single_media_redirect filter; neutralising it for one request gives a 200 native page with h1, og:image, og:title, twitter:card, a 200 image/webp asset and 6 reaction buttons. (2) E.group-dm cites /mvs-pro/v1/groups/{id}/messages - that route does not exist; group creation is /mvs-pro/v1/groups and messaging goes through Free's /mvs/v1/conversations/{id}/messages. A non-member gets 404, not 403. (3) The Fixture cleanup block deletes mvs_reports WHERE reason LIKE 'smoke-%', but reason is an enum so that clause can never match - the marker belongs in details. (4) C.member.video-poster-fallback names PosterService::is_ffmpeg_available(), which does not exist; PosterService has only dir(), stage_bytes() and stage_client_frame(). (5) D.documents-privacy-vocabulary asserts PRIVACY_VALUES is exactly private/members/public - it is now private/space/members/public. The guarded bug is gone: nothing offers 'unlisted', and unlisted or restricted both answer 400 mvs_document_privacy_invalid. (6) C.member.lightbox-edit-modal says the Edit cog appears ONLY on /my-media/ cards - an owner also sees it in the Explore lightbox for their own media, which is not a leak (non-owner gets display:none, and PUT and DELETE answer 403). (7) C.member.bulk-trash-restore-delete describes Move to Trash plus a Trashed filter on /my-media/ - the member bulk bar offers Set privacy, Add to album, Add tags and Delete; trash lives on admin All Media. (8) A3/A4 should state that the competition routes and the /compete/ page depend on competitions being enabled, which is NOT the default (mvs_competitions_enabled ships '0'), otherwise a correct fresh install reads as four 404s and a missing page.
